name: Anabolic steroids for voice

lead: Anabolic steroids and testosterone can lower the voice because they masculinize the larynx. Some people in appearance communities pursue this effect.
Medical sources list it as a side effect, and no trials test steroids as a voice treatment.

paras: Androgens act on the androgen receptor, including in laryngeal tissue, thickening and lengthening the vocal folds in the way male puberty does.
Documented risks include irreversible virilization in women, acne, hair loss, fertility suppression, lipid and liver effects, and legal restrictions as controlled substances.

lead: Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) are synthetic androgens that, like testosterone, can lower the voice by acting on the larynx. Voice deepening is listed among the virilizing effects of testosterone and its esters, and in women it is reported as a possible effect of androgens.[1][2][3]

Some people in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles reportedly view androgens as a way to obtain a deeper voice. Medical sources describe voice deepening as a side effect of treatment, not an indication, and note that androgen-related masculinization in women can be irreversible.[3]
Published material directly on using steroids to change the voice is sparse. A 1964 French-language article titled on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice exists in the literature.[4]

paras: The long-acting ester testosterone cypionate lists deepening of the voice among its virilizing effects, alongside acne and increased body and facial hair.[1] Testosterone more broadly can cause voice deepening in women.[2] Oxandrolone's article describes voice deepening among masculinizing effects in women and states some masculinizing changes can be irreversible.[3]
Adult male vocal folds are longer than female ones, which is associated with lower male pitch.[5]

Androgens carry other documented risks, including acne, hair loss, suppressed sperm production, effects on blood lipids and the liver (particularly oral 17-alkylated agents), and use is contraindicated in pregnancy.[1][2][3] They are controlled substances in the United States.[1]
No studies found of anabolic steroids used for voice goals. Related literature on androgen effects on the voice exists, including a 1964 article on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice.[4]
